world.coords: x right, y down, origin top-left

_format.cells: All scene cell lists are flat arrays of [x,y] pairs in absolute world coordinates.
_format.specimenCells: Specimens use BOTH: `cells` = row-major 0/1 array of width*height, and `rle` = an RLE body string. Specimen coordinates are pattern-local (0,0 = top-left of bounding box).
_format.ascii: ASCII renders use '.' for dead and '#' for alive, rows newline-separated. Whole-world renders use a 2x2 downsample with the ramp ' .:*#' (0-4 live cells per 2x2 block).
_format.cameras: centerX/centerY in cell coordinates; pxPerCell is zoom for a 1440x900 viewport.

opening.title: Opening
opening.description: A distant machine in the top-left corner fires a steady procession of gliders. A dense garden of still lifes and oscillators pulses in the top-right. Two travellers cross the empty southern expanse and meet.

garden.contents: 4x block, 3x beehive, 3x loaf, 3x blinker, 2x boat, 2x tub, 2x pond, 2x ship, 2x toad, 2x beacon, 1x pulsar, 1x pentadecathlon, 1x clock
garden.note: garden state at gen 0 is bit-identical to gen 30; no two objects interact

emptyExpanse.note: entirely empty at gen 0; the encounter happens here

encounter.outcome: The two travellers annihilate each other as ships and bloom into a chaotic reaction that settles (by gen ~1200) into 5 blinkers, 6 blocks and 2 ponds, population 55.

encounter.note: frames the encounter bbox x[107..139] y[91..115] with generous margin (55x35 cells visible)

verification.onlyInteractionThroughGen260: gen 123 — comparing the composite world against garden/gun/travellers evolved independently, the FIRST and ONLY divergence through gen 260 begins at cell (123,94)
verification.crossGroupInteraction: none through gen 260 (gun gliders never reach the garden or the debris)
verification.wrap: no live cell enters the 2-cell border band at any generation 0..300

oneCell.title: One Cell
oneCell.description: A glider is already in flight toward a clock oscillator. Adding a single cell to the edge of the clock decides whether the meeting produces a growing debris field or wipes the world clean.
oneCell.baseComposition: glider at (121..123, 73..75) heading south-east, clock oscillator at (129..132, 88..91)

divergence.note: gen 43, the moment the two futures visibly part (36x22 cells visible)

gen200.note: frames the base future's gen-200 debris field, bbox x[91..151] y[61..108] (80x50 cells visible)

oneCell.qualitativeDifference: Adding one cell at (128,89) sterilises the collision: the flipped future is COMPLETELY EXTINCT (0 live cells anywhere on the torus) from generation 54 onward, while the untouched base future ignites into a still-growing 221-cell debris field of 13 objects that has ejected 3 gliders by generation 200.

runnersUp.note: both futures survive; large population / glider-count split
both futures survive; large population / glider-count split

firstContact.title: First Contact
firstContact.description: A glider drifting south-east and a lightweight spaceship running due west approach across 90 cells of empty space, visibly separated for 115 generations, and meet.

approach.note: horizontal gap in cells between the two bounding boxes

outcome.description: A traffic light: four blinkers in a 9x9 box, period 2, born where the two ships were.

intervention.effect: One extra cell above the lightweight spaceship destroys it. Population falls from 15 to 5 by generation 20; the LWSS is gone, there is no collision at gen 116, and the glider crosses the empty field alone forever.

establishing.note: gen 0: both travellers and the whole approach corridor visible (120x75 cells)

collision.note: frames the collision bbox x[122..136] y[74..92] (48x30 cells visible)

verification.collisionDetection: composite world compared each generation against the two ships evolved independently; first divergence gen 116
verification.wrap: minimum distance from the live bounding box to the torus edge over gens 0..400 is 49 cells
verification.outcomeStable: verified at gen 400: 4 separate period-2 oscillators of 3 cells each

keepAlive.activityDefinition: cells inside rect that changed state during the last 8 generations
keepAlive.solutionDescriptionAtGen150: A real glider is flying. Completing the missing nose cell at (129,60) turns the 4-cell stub into a genuine SE-bound glider (period 4, dx +1 dy +1 per period). At gen 150 it is a clean 5-cell glider with its bounding box at (165,98), still travelling south-east across the empty right half of the rect; it does not reach the rect edge until gen 165. The rest of the frame is the burnt-out soup: 4 blocks that stopped changing at gen 85. Activity through gens ~90-150 is a constant 15 = the cells the moving glider turns on/off inside each 8-generation window.

notes.exhaustiveSingleFlipSearch: all 1806 single-cell toggles in bbox(base)+3 = x91..133,y58..99 were tested; 90 of them keep activity>0 through gen 150, 41 of those also keep every live cell inside R through gen 150. Minimum edit count is therefore 1.
notes.containment: no live cell ever leaves the measurement rect in the baseline (checked to gen 260) nor in the solution before gen 165; the rect is 88x48 inside a 256x160 torus, so nothing wraps and nothing re-enters.

specimens.name: block
specimens.explanation: Four cells in a square; the smallest and most common still life.

specimens.name: beehive
specimens.explanation: A six-cell hexagonal still life, the second most common ash object.

specimens.name: loaf
specimens.explanation: A seven-cell still life shaped like a beehive with a tail.

specimens.name: boat
specimens.explanation: A five-cell still life; the only five-cell still life besides its reflections.

specimens.name: tub
specimens.explanation: Four cells in a diamond, the smallest still life with a hole.

specimens.name: ship
specimens.explanation: A six-cell still life; two boats fused along a diagonal.

specimens.name: pond
specimens.explanation: An eight-cell still life with a 2x2 hole.

specimens.name: blinker
specimens.explanation: Three cells that flip between horizontal and vertical every generation.

specimens.name: toad
specimens.explanation: Two offset rows of three that breathe in and out.

specimens.name: beacon
specimens.explanation: Two diagonally touching blocks whose inner corners blink off and on.

specimens.name: clock
specimens.explanation: A six-cell period-2 oscillator whose arms rotate a quarter turn.

specimens.name: pulsar
specimens.explanation: A large, highly symmetric period-3 oscillator; the most common of its period.

specimens.name: pentadecathlon
specimens.explanation: A period-15 oscillator that stretches and pinches along its long axis.

specimens.name: glider
specimens.explanation: The smallest spaceship: five cells that walk one square diagonally every four generations.

specimens.name: lwss
specimens.explanation: Lightweight spaceship: nine cells travelling two squares orthogonally every four generations.

specimens.name: mwss
specimens.explanation: Middleweight spaceship: an LWSS with one extra bump, same speed.

specimens.name: hwss
specimens.explanation: Heavyweight spaceship: the largest of the three classic orthogonal ships.

specimens.name: gosper-glider-gun
specimens.explanation: Two shuttles whose collision debris condenses into a new glider every 30 generations.

specimens.name: simkin-glider-gun
specimens.explanation: A gun built from four blocks and two shuttles that fires one glider every 120 generations.

specimens.name: r-pentomino
specimens.explanation: Five cells that churn for over a thousand generations before settling.

specimens.name: acorn
specimens.explanation: Seven cells that take more than five thousand generations to settle.

specimens.name: diehard
specimens.explanation: Seven cells that thrash for 130 generations and then vanish completely.

specimens.name: b-heptomino
specimens.explanation: A seven-cell methuselah that settles quickly compared to its cousins.

specimens.name: pi-heptomino
specimens.explanation: A seven-cell methuselah with a longer, showier burn than the b-heptomino.

engine.stillLifes: block, beehive, loaf, boat, tub, ship, pond all detected as period-1 still lifes
engine.oscillators: blinker 2, toad 2, beacon 2, clock 2, pulsar 3, pentadecathlon 15 — all as expected
engine.glider: explicit check: bbox corner (10,10) at gen 0 -> (11,11) at gen 4, i.e. (+1,+1) per 4 generations
engine.gosperGun: gun-body region hash identical at gens 60/90/120/150/180 (period 30); cells outside the gun body increase by exactly 5 every 30 gens from gen 120 to 300
engine.simkinGun: population increases by exactly 5 every 120 gens over gens 600-1200 on an unbounded grid
engine.rPentominoInfinite: on an 800x800 grid population is 116 at gen 1103 and stays exactly 116 through gen 1400 — matches the literature value
engine.rPentominoOnThisTorus: DISCREPANCY: on the 256x160 torus the escaping gliders wrap and re-enter. Populations: gen 100=121, 500=174, 1000=156, 1103=116, 2000=112, 3000=109. It enters a period-2 cycle at generation 2189 with population 109. It does NOT freeze at gen 1103.
engine.acorn: unbounded grid: stabilises at gen 5206 with population 633 (peak 1057 at gen 4408) — matches the literature value
engine.diehard: unbounded grid: dies completely at gen 130 — matches the literature value

opening.method: the composite world was stepped alongside the garden, the gun and the two travellers evolved in separate worlds; every generation the composite was compared cell-by-cell against the union of the parts
opening.firstDivergence: gen 123 at cell (123,94) — this is the intended encounter and the only divergence through gen 260
opening.crossGroup: zero divergence between the composite and (garden ∪ gun ∪ travellers-as-one-group) through gen 260, so the gun gliders never touch the garden or the debris
opening.wrap: no live cell enters the 2-cell border band at any generation 0..300
opening.gardenIndependence: garden-only world: hash at gen 0 == hash at gen 30, so no two garden objects interact

oneCell.searchedBy: subagent brute force; RE-AUDITED independently by /tmp/afterlife-scenes/audit.mjs
oneCell.extinctionGen: the flipped future has zero live cells anywhere on the torus from generation 54 onward
oneCell.wrap: the base future never comes within 3 cells of the torus edge through gen 200

firstContact.collisionDetection: composite compared each generation against the glider and the LWSS evolved independently; first divergence gen 116
firstContact.outcomeAtGen400: 4 objects, each a 3-cell period-2 oscillator (a traffic light), total population 12 in a 9x9 box at x[118..126] y[85..93]
firstContact.interventionVerified: toggling (188,74) dead->alive drops the population from 15 to 5 by gen 20 and the only surviving object at gen 400 is a single period-4 glider
firstContact.wrap: minimum distance from the live bounding box to the torus edge over gens 0..400 is 49 cells

keepAlive.searchedBy: subagent exhaustive single-cell search; RE-AUDITED independently by /tmp/afterlife-scenes/audit.mjs
keepAlive.auditResult: baseline activity first reaches 0 at generation 85 and is 0 at every generation from there through 200; with the single edit (129,60) dead->alive the minimum activity over generations 8..150 is 15, i.e. > 0 everywhere
keepAlive.wrap: the solution run never leaves the measurement rect through gen 150

specimens.method: every still life / oscillator / spaceship was placed alone on a padded grid and run until its state repeated; the returned period and bbox displacement are reported. Emitters and seeds were run on an unbounded sparse grid.
specimens.dropped: period-N puffer — DROPPED, could not verify one. 2,640 LWSS+LWSS+b-heptomino arrangements were searched and the 73 showing sustained growth were long-run to gen 2000; none was a clean periodic puffer. Two remembered block-laying-switch-engine RLEs also failed (populations settled to constants 61 and 83).
